messages:
Nadia (Security): Important: we discovered multiple customer buckets with overly permissive ACLs and cross-account writes. We're rolling out an automated bucket-policy enforcement that will block PUBLIC and external-account writes unless exempted. Action required by teams owning affected buckets by 2026-04-07. Link: https://redwood.internal/sec/s3-policy-enforce :rotating_light:
s3-bot: Scan result summary: 37 buckets flagged across prod registries. Affected teams: payments, exports, telemetry-extracts. Full report: https://go.redwood/reports/s3-scan-1814004321
Nadia (Security): High-level steps: 1) review the report for your team's buckets 2) remove public ACLs and replace with org-only policies 3) if cross-account writes are needed, file an exception with justification + reviewer list by 2026-04-05.
Omar (Storage): Enforcement details: On 2026-04-08 at 00:00 UTC we'll enable a mutating webhook that will patch offending bucket policies to block PublicAccess and deny PutObject from non-org principals. In dry-run mode from 2026-04-03.
Jake (SRE): Will this affect backup exports that write to vendor buckets for analytics?
Nadia (Security): Yes - those are cross-account writes. Options: 1) move exports to org-owned destination 2) set up explicit cross-account IAM role with least privilege and register the delegation in the "crossaccount-registry". Exemptions are temporary and require rotation plan.
Lin (DevOps): Example remediation policy snippet to add to buckets (JSON):
```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::your-bucket/*","Condition":{"StringNotEquals":{"aws:PrincipalOrgID":"o-abc123"}}}
  ]
}
```
Hannah (Compliance): Reminder: customer PII cannot be stored in any bucket with public ACLs. Teams with flagged buckets that store PII must complete a data classification review by 2026-04-01.
s3-bot: Actionable flags: buckets with public-read ACL (12), buckets with public-write ACL (5), cross-account put permissions (20). See per-bucket notes in the report.
Omar (Storage): We're providing a one-click remediation script in infra-tools that will apply the org-only deny and create a ticket in the owner's tracker. Use with caution; it will invalidate some 3rd-party workflows.
Jake (SRE): What's the rollback plan if the webhook causes app regressions?
Omar (Storage): In dry-run we'll gather webhook findings. During enforcement we'll patch with a reversible label; infra-bot can revert policy to previous state for a 2-hour window if critical. We'll coordinate with oncall.
Lin (DevOps): CI helper: rctl s3-check --bucket=your-bucket will show flagged ACLs and suggest commands. Example fix: aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket your-bucket --acl private && aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket your-bucket --policy file://org-deny.json
s3-bot: Reminder scheduled: dry-run starts 2026-04-03 00:00 UTC. Enforcement planned 2026-04-08 00:00 UTC. Office hours: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC in #eng-all.
Hannah (Compliance): If you believe your bucket is a false positive (eg transient public for CDN), document the reason in the report and attach a mitigation/TTL. We will not approve permanent public ACLs for customer data.
Nadia (Security): Please ack in-thread when you've checked your team's buckets and filed any needed exception requests. If you need help, ping @Nadia or join the office hours. :lock:
